newsitem.title: BOSNIA: EU grants $7.4 million to rid Bosnia of land mines.
newsitem.headline: EU grants $7.4 million to rid Bosnia of land mines.

text.p: The European Union announced a $7.4 million grant on Friday to rid postwar Bosnia of land mines which have killed or wounded hundreds of people.
The money will fund the purchase of mine clearance equipment, salaries for 240 mine-removal personnel in up to 20 teams and the establishment of a rapid-reaction Explosive Ordnance Disposal Unit.

"It will be the first comprehensive, countrywide de-mining programme, signed with the Bosnian federation and (Bosnian) Serb republic governments," said NATO peace force spokesman Lieutenant Colonel Max Marriner.
An EU statement said Bosnia bristled with up to three million mines laid by Serb, Moslem and Croat armies during 43 months of nationalist war that ended with the Dayton peace treaty in late 1995.
It said around 100 mine casualties were reported every month with Sarajevo's Kosevo Hospital admitting on average one seriously injured mine victim a day.
NATO peace force engineers have identified only about half the country's minefields so far.
"The European Commission recognises that (mines) will be a long-term deterrent to (economic) regeneration in many areas," the EU statement said.
"(So), since opening its office in Sarajevo earlier this year, it has made de-mining a priority funding target."
The EU programme will contract specialised de-mining companies to train local personnel, probably unemployed demobilised soldiers.
